solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excellent position when supine?

indicators.note: supine means lying on the back, so in a down clue the word for position is turned over and reads upwards

parts.note: a spot is a place or position

explanation.surface: Lying flat on one's back must be the ideal posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something described as the best of all is excellent.

clue.text: Proposal made by Top Cat from the floor?

indicators.note: reading from the floor up in a down clue means the phrase is reversed

parts.note: the best tom is number one, NO I TOM

explanation.surface: A motion tabled by the cartoon character Top Cat, raised from the floor of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Cat is NO I TOM (number one tom); read from the floor upward it gives the answer. 'From the floor' also suggests a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: In a meeting or debate, a formal proposal put to the vote has this name.

clue.text: Details of 'Westbound' couple grabbing kiss in Glasgow?

indicators.note: bound means wrapped round, so the actress's name binds the other letters

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress, so West gives her first name

indicators.note: grabbing means holding inside, so the pair of ones holds the kiss

parts.note: a couple is two, II in Roman numerals
a Glasgow kiss is a headbutt, which is to nut someone

explanation.surface: Fine points about a westbound couple stealing a kiss in a Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'Westbound' must be split: the actress Mae West's first name is bound round the rest. A Glasgow kiss is British slang for a headbutt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means tiny precise particulars, the small points of anything.

clue.text: Carrot, perhaps, all bar the top for Dennis Rodman

indicators.note: all bar means everything except, so a letter is dropped from the carrot word

parts.note: a carrot dangled as an incentive is an example of a dangler

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, here of Dennis

explanation.surface: A clue seemingly about the basketball star Dennis Rodman and some carrot-topped hair.
explanation.walkthrough: DANGLER, as in carrot and stick, loses D, the top of 'Dennis'. Dennis Rodman is a US basketball player, but 'Rodman' is read as rod man.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as rod plus man, a rodman is someone who fishes with a rod.

clue.text: Counterpoised among unusual enemies, old Greek king

indicators.note: counterpoised suggests a balancing opposite direction, so the letters run backwards
among says the letters lie within the words unusual enemies

explanation.surface: A legendary Greek ruler holds the balance amid strange foes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' finds SUALENEM inside 'unusual enemies' and 'Counterpoised' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The King of Sparta whose wife Helen was taken to Troy, sparking the Trojan War.

clue.text: Screen brought to court erected around back of prisoner

indicators.note: around means the reversed phrase is set round the prisoner's last letter
erected means raised upright, so in a down clue the phrase is read upwards

parts.note: to be had up is to be brought before a court

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of the word prisoner

explanation.surface: A screen is hauled into court and set up around a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: HAD UP, 'erected', gives PUDAH, which goes 'around' R, the back of 'prisoner'.
explanation.definitionFit: The practice of screening women from men or strangers, and the curtain used to do so.

clue.text: Hats off to South Africa's rugby adjudicator

indicators.note: hats are worn at the top, so the head letters come off the following words

explanation.surface: A salute to the referee of South African rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hats off' looks like praise but takes the first letters of 'to South Africa's rugby'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely, an appointed overseer with power to rule on matters, like a drugs or tennis supremo.

clue.text: Bans missing mass by Northern priest

indicators.note: missing means the abbreviation for mass is left out of the word for bans

parts.note: moratoria, plural of moratorium, are bans or suspensions
M is the physics abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A list of prohibitions, with Mass dropped, imposed by a priest from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing mass' takes M from MORATORIA, leaving ORATORIA, which then gets N beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Oratory, the congregation founded by St Philip Neri, is a priest of that order.

clue.text: An absorbing paper under discussion

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A
tissue is soft paper used to soak things up

explanation.surface: An engrossing newspaper article on a topical subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' looks like engrossing, but it means soaking up: a TISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter being debated or in dispute is said to be at issue, an idiom.

clue.text: Eratosthenes' First Question: American play

indicators.note: First here signals that only the opening letter of the Greek mathematician's name is used

parts.note: US stands for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A grand-sounding title for the first problem posed by the Greek mathematician Eratosthenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American play' looks like one phrase, but American supplies US and the definition is just 'play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Shaffer wrote a celebrated stage drama of that Latin title, about a boy who blinds horses.

clue.text: Guru's rest interrupted by solemn goings-on on meadow

indicators.note: a word broken into by other letters has them placed within it, so the rest word is split open

parts.note: a spider is a snooker rest, a cue support with long legs for reaching over balls
a ritual is a solemn ceremonial proceeding
lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: A guru's quiet time is disturbed by some ceremony taking place on a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' is the snooker SPIDER, a cue support, not repose. Snooker is a British cue game like pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A guru is a religious teacher who guides followers in matters of the soul and faith.

clue.text: Contemptible, the state of Elizabeth I's growler

parts.note: base means low, mean or contemptible
Elizabeth is a city in New Jersey, abbreviated NJ

explanation.surface: The despicable condition of Queen Elizabeth I's snarling hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elizabeth I' points to the Tudor queen, but Elizabeth is a city in New Jersey, giving the state abbreviation NJ.
explanation.definitionFit: A basenji is an African hunting dog breed which cannot bark but can growl and yodel, so it is a growler by elimination.

clue.text: Man perhaps shows very little change between the sheets

indicators.note: between puts the small change in the middle of the word for sheets

parts.note: between the sheets is in bed
1p, one penny, is very little change, written IP

explanation.surface: A man shows how little he has changed while in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man perhaps' is the definition by example; very little change is one penny, written with the numeral as a letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans walk on two legs, so a man is an example of a two-footed animal.

clue.text: Terribly hard when negotiating roundabout to pass around … him?

indicators.note: negotiating a roundabout means going round it, so the rearranged letters surround the round letter
terribly signals the word hard is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: a roundabout is circular, like the letter O

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for pass the other way

parts.note: to go is to pass or proceed

explanation.surface: Someone driving recklessly round a roundabout, cutting across to overtake: who else could it be?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges the four letters of hard around the round letter; 'around' turns the word for pass backwards. The ellipsis and 'him?' point to the culprit the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the aggressive selfish motorist, with him standing for that driver.

clue.text: Two thirds of University course complete, leaving one longing for more

indicators.note: two thirds of a six-letter word means its first two letters are dropped

parts.note: a degree is a university course of study

indicators.note: leaving means taking out the word one from the word for complete

parts.note: done means complete, finished
one is taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A student two-thirds of the way through a degree is eager to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: DEGREE keeps two thirds, GREE; DONE leaving ONE gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is the vice of always wanting more than one needs.

clue.text: First of price indexes — what 12ac may be after market priority

indicators.note: First of signals taking only the opening letter of the word price

parts.note: an index lists references, so indexes can be references
12 across is a hunting dog breed, which might chase a hare

explanation.surface: An economic report on the leading price indicators, and what a hunting dog chases.
explanation.walkthrough: The 12ac basenji is a hunting dog, so what it may be after is its quarry, a HARE.
explanation.definitionFit: This class of stock gives holders priority over ordinary shareholders on the stock market for dividends.

clue.text: Coming round bend, almost empty lungs of bishop

indicators.note: coming round means the shortened word for emptying lungs wraps around the curve
almost means the final letter of the breathing word is dropped

parts.note: to exhale is to empty one's lungs
an arc is a bend or curve

explanation.surface: A bishop rounds a corner and breathes out hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the breathing word to EXHAL. 'of bishop' is adjectival: exarchs are bishops in the Eastern churches.
explanation.definitionFit: An exarch is a senior prelate in Eastern Orthodoxy, so this adjective relates to such an overseer.

clue.text: Supply machine with new balls

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, supply means in a pliant way, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Load a bowling machine with fresh balls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is read as the adverb of supple, rearranging MACHINE with N. In cricket these are left-arm spin deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a left-arm wrist-spinner's deliveries turning into a right-hander are known by this term.

clue.text: Unjustifiably claimed this laser can upset 24ac

indicators.note: upset means jumbled, so this word plus laser and can are rearranged into the long across entry

parts.note: 24 across is the dodgy car dealer

explanation.surface: Somebody falsely claimed a laser could unsettle a dodgy car dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus LASER and CAN, 'upset', make USED-CAR SALESMAN, so remove LASER and CAN from those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken for granted without proof has been presumed, claimed without justification.

clue.text: Brown had B, Cameron had C, but this is upsetting!

definitions.text: Brown had B, Cameron had C, but this is upsetting!

parts.words: Brown had B, Cameron had C, but this is upsetting!
parts.note: the British prime ministers Gordon Brown and David Cameron were followed by Theresa May; continuing the letter sequence, the next letter D is hers

explanation.surface: A political commentator lamenting the plans of successive prime ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as D IS MAY'S: after B and C comes D, belonging to Theresa May, the next prime minister. Brown, Cameron and May were successive UK prime ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upsetting causes alarm and distress, which is what the verb in the answer means.

clue.text: Plain, bare skin and bones of Sgt Pepper?

indicators.note: the bare skin of a word is just its outside letters, here of Sgt
the bones are the inner part, so the middle of Pepper without its ends

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to be about the Beatles' Sgt Pepper looking scrawny.
explanation.walkthrough: The skin of 'Sgt' is ST and the bones of 'Pepper' are EPPE, its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast treeless grassland of Eurasia is a flat plain.

clue.text: Jacques Clouseau our ultimate offbeat detective? Ultimately, yes

definitions.text: Jacques Clouseau our ultimate offbeat detective? Ultimately, yes

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the first six words of the clue

parts.words: Jacques Clouseau our ultimate offbeat detective

explanation.surface: Is Inspector Clouseau our quirkiest sleuth? In the end, yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Clouseau, of the Pink Panther films, is a French detective, so the French police force fits the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French national detective department, where the bumbling inspector served.

clue.text: I treated dioxides, volatile, with variable light

indicators.note: volatile, unstable and changeable, signals the letters are shaken into a new order
light here means lacking, so the variable is dropped from the word dioxides

parts.note: X is the classic algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A chemist's lab note about treating some unstable dioxides with light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' means short of: DIOXIDES loses X, the variable, and 'volatile' rearranges DIOIDES. 'I' is the chemical symbol for iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: Table salt is commonly treated with iodine, chemical symbol I, so it is described this way.

clue.text: Fanciful predecessor of PM entering nut repository?

indicators.note: entering means the morning letters go inside the nest

parts.note: a drey is a squirrel's nest, where nuts may be stored
AM, morning, comes before PM, afternoon

explanation.surface: A wild idea: a former prime minister hiding in a squirrel's store of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' suggests a Prime Minister, but it is afternoon, preceded by AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fanciful is vague and imaginative, like a reverie.

clue.text: Perhaps Arfur Daley's dubious assurances led the old girl to get sucked in

indicators.note: the old girl getting sucked in means she is drawn inside the rearranged letters
dubious signals that the words assurances led are unreliable and must be rearranged

parts.note: an old girl can be one's mother, MA

explanation.surface: A dodgy dealer's shady promises lured an elderly woman into a bad deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Daley, Cockney 'Arfur', is the wheeler-dealer of the British TV comedy-drama Minder, who sold cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Daley is the archetypal example of a shady second-hand motor trader.

clue.text: State that usually rises to press …

indicators.note: rises in a down clue means the letters read upwards, reversed
to press means to squeeze, so the answer is squeezed within the words

explanation.surface: A state whose output usually goes up just before going to print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to press' finds HATU inside 'that usually' and 'rises' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a US state in the Mountain West, capital Salt Lake City.

clue.text: … twisting ends of story is not American

indicators.note: twisting the ends of the word for story means its first and last letters change places

parts.note: a yarn is a story

explanation.surface: Twisting the end of a tale is not the American way.
explanation.walkthrough: YARN swaps its ends, Y and N, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This dialect word, as in 'nary a one', means not any, chiefly in US usage.

clue.text: A broadcast record the penny drops to secure

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the exclamation encloses the record

parts.note: aha is what one says when the penny drops, in sudden understanding
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A radio show plays a record and the listener finally understands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A broadcast' means the letter A as spoken in radio transmissions. 'The penny drops' is a British idiom for suddenly understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet used over the radio, the letter A is said as this word.

clue.text: Ascetic's time to move forward in anticipation of golden month

indicators.note: to move forward means the time letter is shifted to the front of the ascetic

parts.note: a hermit is an ascetic living in solitude
d'or is French for of gold, golden

explanation.surface: A recluse's hour comes ahead of a month of plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move forward' shifts T to the front, giving THERMI; 'in anticipation of' places it before the French for golden, d'or.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the eleventh month of the French Revolutionary calendar, roughly late July to August.
